1.explanation:
• ListBoxSelection.js is responsible for Carbon’s live-region announcements of the currently focused/selected item.  It always renders a live-region that announces the item text plus “selected (n of m)”.

• ListBox.js composes ListBoxSelection alongside the menu and does not distinguish single-select dropdowns from multi-select or combobox variants, so for a basic single-select it still emits that live announcement.

• Dropdown.js is the top-level component that uses ListBox under the hood.  It doesn’t disable or override the secondary announcement, so end users hear the same text twice: once from the native focus announcement and again from the custom live region.

To fix this, you need to adjust ListBox and/or Dropdown so that for a simple single-select dropdown you suppress the extra live-region announcement in ListBoxSelection, avoiding the duplicate readout.
1.bug_scenario: When you open a Carbon <Dropdown> on macOS 11.1 with Safari and VoiceOver enabled (⌘-F5), VO will read each item twice as you arrow through the menu.  The first announcement comes from the native reading of the focused <li role="option">.  The second comes from Carbon’s custom live-region announcement (built into ListBoxSelection) that repeats the text and adds “selected (n of m)”.  The result is “Option 4 Option 4, selected (5 of 6)”.

2.explanation:
1. packages/react/src/components/Dropdown/Dropdown.js  
   • This is the entry point for the React <Dropdown> component. It passes down default Downshift props (including the built-in getA11yStatusMessage for announcing selection changes) alongside Carbon’s own a11y handling. Misconfiguration here means both Carbon’s and Downshift’s announcements fire, leading to duplicate reads.  
2. packages/react/src/components/ListBox/ListBox.js  
   • ListBox wraps Downshift and wires up both aria-activedescendant and a polite aria-live region for announcing focus and selection state. Because it doesn’t suppress Downshift’s default status messages when Carbon also renders its own, VoiceOver receives two separate announcements for each navigation event.  
3. packages/react/src/components/ListBox/ListBoxMenuItem.js  
   • The individual <ListBoxMenuItem> injects visually-hidden text for the highlighted item (to read out its text and selection position), while the element’s visible text is also present. VoiceOver therefore reads the same text twice (once from the visible content and once from the hidden region) before reading the listbox status, compounding the duplication.
2.bug_scenario: On macOS 11.1 with Safari and VoiceOver enabled (⌘ F5), navigating through the Carbon React <Dropdown> options causes each option to be announced twice: once for the visible label and once again for the assistive-technology-only status message showing “<OptionText>, selected (n of n)”. In Storybook’s a11y panel this shows up as the merged overlay “Option 4 Option 4, selected (5 of 6)”.
